summary: Enter or update data directly within a grid or table interface, optionally adding new rows, and commit the changes.
preconditions: A grid, spreadsheet, or table editor interface is open on the screen.
steps: If entering a new record and no empty row is available, click the button to add a new row.
Click directly inside the target cell to activate its input field.
Type the desired value into the active cell.
Repeat the click-and-type process for all other cells requiring updates.
Click the save button (typically labeled 'Save Changes' or similar) to commit the edits to the database.

variants.do: Omit the final save button click, as changes are committed upon deselecting the cell or pressing Enter.

variants.when: data needs to be copied from another source tab
variants.do: Switch to the source tab, copy or note the value, switch back to the grid tab, and type it into the active cell.

watch_for: The cell input field displaying a cursor or highlight border, indicating it is ready for typing.
The typed text appearing correctly inside the cell boundaries.
completion_signal: A success notification appears, or the save button becomes temporarily disabled, indicating all changes have been successfully committed.
pitfalls: Clicking away from an active cell before finishing typing, which may discard the uncommitted cell value.
Forgetting to click the final save button in interfaces that do not support autosave.
